Breaking: US and UK to host Women's World Cups in 2031 and 2035

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (360 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • FIFA have confirmed the hosts for the 2031 and 2035 Women's World Cup.
  • The United States, along with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica, made an uncontested bid to host in 2031.
  • FIFA's revenue for the 2026 men's World Cup was around $15 billion (€13.7 billion), and it's clear that US Soccer feels that hosting the women's tournament is the next move forward.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

FIFA have confirmed the hosts for the 2031 and 2035 Women's World Cup.

The United States, along with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica, made an uncontested bid to host in 2031. It will be the first tournament to feature 48 teams — as is the case with the men. The US has hosted the event twice before, in 2003 and 1999, and is also the most successful country in its history, having won it four times.

FIFA's revenue for the 2026 men's World Cup was around $15 billion (€13.7 billion), and it's clear that US Soccer feels that hosting the women's tournament is the next move forward. With the women's domestic league (NWSL) considered the strongest in the world and the US national team so dominant, securing the tournament in 2031 is a further sign of the US' committment to women's football.

"We expect and initiative for the 2031 Women’s World Cup to be the largest women’s sporting event in history," Emily Cosler, US Soccer’s vice-president of strategy told The Guardian.

The 2035 tournament was also awarded to the sole bidders, England, Scotland, Northern Ireland and Wales. This sees the World Cup return to the United Kingdom for the first time since 1966, the only time England's men's team won the competition. The women lost the 2023 final to Spain. It also means that the UK will host two major tournaments in relatively quick succession, with the men's 2028 European Championships also set to be held in England, Scotland and Wales and the Republic of Ireland.

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham noted the tournament would bring "visitors, investment and jobs to every part of the country.".

Sources indicate that given that FIFA President Gianni Infantino had revealed last year that both bids were unchallenged, this news comes as little surprise. Nevertheless, with the hosts now official, a 48-team tournament marks a remarkable advance for the women's game. The 2011 World Cup in Germany had just 16 teams.

The next World Cup will be in Brazil in 2027, running from June 24 to July 25. . Eighteen of the 32 teams have already secured qualification, including Germany.

Some fans whistle as Lionel Messi's name is declared as Paris Saint-Germain's season hits new low

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Paris Saint-Germain’s miserable season went from bad to worse on Sunday as the team suffered a second straight home defeat with a 1-0 loss to Lyon.
  • Even before the game kicked off, Lionel Messi bore the brunt of the frustrations of some PSG fans who whistled when his name appeared on the big screen during the announcement of the starting lineup.
  • Lionel Messi passes 100 international goals with hat-trick against Curaçao.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Paris Saint-Germain’s miserable season went from bad to worse on Sunday as the team suffered a second straight home defeat with a 1-0 loss to Lyon.

Even before the game kicked off, Lionel Messi bore the brunt of the frustrations of some PSG fans who whistled when his name appeared on the big screen during the announcement of the starting lineup.

Lionel Messi passes 100 international goals with hat-trick against Curaçao.

After Alexadre Lacazette missed a first-half penalty, Bradley Barcola’s goal 10 minutes into the second period was enough to earn Lyon the three points on a night that PSG rarely looked like threatening the visiting goal.

Lens’ 1-0 victory over Rennes and Marseille’s 1-1 draw with Montepellier means both teams are now just six points behind PSG at the top of Ligue 1, and even the domestic title may slip from the team’s grasp.

The reaction of some fans on Sunday must have felt a world away from the adulation and worship Messi received during his recent return to Argentina for friendlies against Panama and Curaçao as the country continued its World Cup celebrations.

Messi’s arrival at the Parc des Princes was supposed to be the missing piece that would help PSG finally win the Champions League, the trophy the club’s Qatari owners crave the most.

So far, the only major trophy the team has won since Messi joined was Ligue 1 last season, a title – it’s fair to say – PSG would likely have won without him.

Messi has 34 goal contributions in all competitions for PSG this season – 18 goals and 17 assists – second only to Mbappé’s 38 and head coach Christophe Galtier refused to lay the blame for the team’s failures at the Argentine’s feet.

“I found it [the jeering] hard to listen to,” Galtier told reporters, per the Athletic. “There may be expectations for Messi and Mbappe to unlock difficult situations. Messi tries very hard, they didn’t all work out; but around him, the other players also need to do their jobs.”.

“We can’t expect everything from Leo and Kylian,” he added.

Lionel Messi mania grips Argentina as World Cup celebrations continue.

Up next for PSG is a season-defining week as Galtier’s side travels to a Nice team that is unbeaten in 13 matches, before hosting Lens at the Parc des Princes.

PSG has lost two of its three matches since being dumped out of the Champions League by Bayern Munich last month, and only limped past relegation-threatened Brest with a 90th minute Kylian Mbappé winner.

After his team’s victory, Lyon head coach Laurent Blanc said the Champions League or bust mentality has been detrimental to PSG’s performances.

In a recent development, “Paris’ problem is when the No. 1 objective of the Champions League is no longer accessible, it seems that the season no longer exists – and at all levels,” he told reporters.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tottenham Hotspur’s resurgence under Roberto De Zerbi has breathed fresh life into the club after back-to-back 17th-placed finishes.

There is one clear deficiency in their current make-up that threatens to limit what they can achieve in 2026/27, though - they can't finish.

Despite sitting comfortably in the top half after 12 games, Spurs’ underlying attacking numbers tell the story of a side creating plenty and squandering too much of it.

Tottenham have rattled off 170 shots in the Premier League this season - the fifth-highest tally in the division - while only Liverpool and Manchester City have registered more efforts from inside the penalty area than Spurs’ 109.

But, when it comes to actually hitting the target, De Zerbi’s side slump to 14th across the top flight.

Recent findings suggest that there's also an concern with their ball-striking. According to Gradient Sports’ analysts, just six of Spurs’ 170 league attempts have been graded as ‘unsaveable’ - a figure bettered by every team in the Premier League bar Everton (5).

For context, high-flying Brighton have racked up 20 unsaveable efforts, while Erling Haaland has managed seven on his own. At 3.5 per cent, Tottenham boast the lowest proportion of unsaveable shots in the entire division.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

A glance at De Zerbi’s attacking options explains why to some extent. Richarlison has been frozen out entirely and is angling for a January move, Dominic Solanke has managed just two league goals, and significant-money summer arrival Omar Marmoush is yet to hit the ground running in north London.

Centre-back Jan Paul van Hecke is the team's joint-top Premier League goalscorer with two goals after 12 matches: Spurs need a centre-forward in January.

Enter Real Sociedad’s 22-year-old Icelandic international Orri Oskarsson.

Oskarsson is by no means LaLiga’s most prolific frontman, having netted four times in the Spanish top flight this term but his underlying metrics point towards a striker ready to thrive in a possession-heavy, attack-minded system.

Unlike De Zerbi’s Spurs, Real Sociedad do not dominate the ball as often, leaving their striker without service for large periods of matches. Oskarsson, though, is making every second count when his team are in possession, averaging a goal every 64 minutes that La Real actually have the ball this season.

In total, he has scored nine times across his last 13 appearances for club and country.

In a recent development, what makes Oskarsson particularly suited to Tottenham is how intelligently he moves to receive the ball. Gradient Sports’ data reveals the Icelandic forward receives line-breaking passes 45 per cent of the time, placing him among LaLiga’s best at peeling off defenders and making himself available to creative midfielders.

That off-the-ball awareness is reinforced by the fact he has received the ball in a clear shooting position 10 times in the league this season - a tally bettered only by Barcelona’s Raphinha (13) and Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe (11).

Once the ball arrives at his feet, Oskarsson has the penalty-box nous Tottenham lack. Ninety-two per cent of his LaLiga shots this season have been taken from inside the box, which aligns nicely with the 109 close-range openings Spurs have already generated this term. Even more impressive, out of the 25 shots he has taken in LaLiga, five have been graded as unsaveable by Gradient's analysts - just one fewer than Tottenham’s entire squad combined.

Gradient have also flagged just one occasion all season where Oskarsson opted to shoot when passing to a better-placed teammate was the superior option, highlighting good judgement under pressure and decision-making that is rare for a 22-year-old.

Meanwhile, his Expected Goals (xG) ranks sixth-highest in LaLiga - a decent return given Real Sociedad’s modest share of possession and chance creation.

It has been revealed that and best of all, a winter deal is entirely plausible. For a Tottenham side creating plenty of penalty-box opportunities but with nobody reliable to tuck them away, Oskarsson could be one of the more shrewd January investments the market has to offer.

#151250. The biggest fear behind the Premier League’s controversial move to digital football tickets

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1619 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

The biggest fear behind the Premier League’s controversial move to digital football tickets

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1619 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later?
  • In a recent development, it is described as the Premier League’s “secret civil war”, except it’s very public.
  • This season’s full introduction of digital tickets has affected fan behaviour and community.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

In a recent development, it is described as the Premier League’s “secret civil war”, except it’s very public. So much so that it affects the majority of those who fill stadiums every single week. It affects the lifeblood of football… but then the entire point is that this isn’t something tangible you can touch.

This season’s full introduction of digital tickets has affected fan behaviour and community.

It has been revealed that you can see it in queues outside games. You can hear it in discussions on the difficulty of “passing on” tickets, and arguably even atmosphere.

Duncan Drasdo of the Manchester United Supporters Trust says, “it absolutely impacts fan culture”.

The Football Supporters’ Association say they are “monitoring” how it progresses but it all plays into a deeper sense, that there is a long-term aim to eventually end season tickets altogether.

Multiple clubs contacted for this article strenuously dispute this, and many are quite strident on their position.

The move comes from a vote in the summer of 2024, where there was effusive support for the mandatory introduction of digital tickets from the start of this season. This essentially means doing away with old physical tickets - although clubs can still give them out in special cases - for ones now scanned. And, if holders can’t go, they can pass to selected family and friends, or put on the club exchange.

Recent findings suggest that there are two primary arguments the clubs make. One is cutting down on touting, which they insist is still absolutely rife. Club sources say the data demonstrated networks where people were running 50-60 season-ticket accounts, and there was financial gain. They argue that runs contrary to the idea of the season ticket being personal to a fan for their loyalty, and insist the only action - achieved through hidden barcodes - is against abuse.

In a recent development, the other is increasing safety, and knowing everyone who is in the stadium. It inherently conditions better behaviour, since anyone can be tracked.

Fan groups accept parts of these arguments, and would acknowledge that a lot of their clubs directly engage, but sympathy has been eroded by direct experience. Almost immediately, there were long queues outside games, many of which have lingered. Most pertinently, though, there is the sudden negating of what has long been normal. Every season-ticket holder will know it, as will those who use their tickets. “Passing on” is a lot more difficult, as clubs increase obligation for the ticket to be used in some form.

“And passing it on is absolutely fan culture,” says Gareth Roberts, of Liverpool’s Spirit of Shankly group. Drasdo adds: “It’s what creates community.”.

A common complaint is that it now involves more laborious processes, and doing it unofficially potentially risks a ban, when you used to be able to just hand it to someone.

In a recent development, “Not just talking about Liverpool here, but I do know of fans who do get worried about it,” Roberts states. “There are so many rules and regulations to take in, it’s almost like taking an exam. It feels a heavy load to be a supporter.

“Through not filling in the initial form as they wanted, I have one mate who can’t go to Champions League games and two who can’t go to cups. The assumption is that everyone is digitally literate, but they don’t.”.

This has practical concerns, too, if a fan can’t go at short notice.

“We’ve been saying there should be ways to do this,” Roberts says. “You’re not setting up a business and earning from this. OK, there are touts but they have to think of ways to not impinge on traditional fans.”.

Industry observers note that darren Epstein, a Gold Rep at Arsenal, indicates the complication of it all is under-appreciated: “In days gone by, we’d be talking about managers and tactics. Now it’s when away tickets go on sale, collections, ID checks, and points - points being the loyalty points you get on buying an away ticket.

According to recent reports, “It feels like a constant battle to ensure you get to a game. Although, changes have undoubtedly improved the ability of many fans to get to games they never have been able to before, which many of course feel is a good thing.”.

A connected complaint is that this is one more factor affecting traditional atmospheres.

“If it’s the club re-selling the ticket on the exchange, it changes the profile of the support, introducing a random fan into a group of mates,” Drasdo says. “In the old standing sections you were able to congregate with friends but the introduction of all-seater stadia meant people got split up by where their seats were and we lost that mobility which is the key to atmosphere.".

Tom Concannon of the FSA, speaking as a Newcastle United fan, notes: “Atmospheres are worsening because of it in my opinion. Tickets are going to those wanting to experience the atmosphere rather than contribute to it.” Roberts adds: “Atmosphere is dependent on youth vibrancy. The Kop is pretty old now.”.

Even in simple terms, it’s a lot harder to pass on tickets to children who may not have a phone, but that clubs actively need to get that match-day buzz. Fan representatives would similarly say it doesn’t help that the Premier League’s clubs’ ticketing working group only has heads of ticketing on it, rather than actual match-going fans.

Such concern feeds into a deeper tension in all of this, between being a supporter and being a customer. An irony is that it means fans have less control over what they pay for. As one executive states, “if you’ve bought your season ticket, you should have no obligation to sit in the seat”.

Another perspective is that clubs are being more strict and trying to get control of every ticket they can. One industry figure points to how the same data from digital tickets has allowed clubs to see just how often tickets are passed on, and it has stunned them. One club has estimated that 20-25 per cent of tickets are passed on, which they also see as running contrary to what a season ticket is supposed to be.

Or, as some fans put, they realised they could monetise. Tickets not passed on can be put on the ticket exchange, where FSA research indicates prices are considerably higher than the average for a season-ticket seat.

Club sources would say they deliberately decoupled the season-ticket price from match-by-match, to recognise the value of a season-ticket holder.

Drasdo offers a different view: “A common phrase we hear from our fans is ‘the club are the biggest touts of all’, which is essentially a reaction to the restrictions on usage and the premium prices we see when season ticket holders' tickets are resold by the club.

“A major problem we’ve had at United is stretching the gap in price between season ticket holders and member ticket prices which causes the club to focus on how season ticket holders pass on their tickets when not personally attending.”.

Sources indicate that another knock-on has been what Roberts describes as the “normalisation” of fans who don’t have season tickets paying fees to become members to go into lotteries for tickets. Some clubs even charge for transferring. Most clubs have unlimited membership, meaning there is actually less chance of getting a ticket.

“We’ll never really know how many tickets end up in the hands of actual fans,” Concannon claims. “Hospitality numbers are on the rise.”.

In a recent development, clubs would nevertheless insist they are acutely conscious of this, and they have to allow opportunities for fans on long waiting lists, or who otherwise feel shut out of being able to go to games. That has fostered tension between supporters, as well as between supporters and clubs. Fans who speak out often find themselves shouted down by others who say “if you don’t pay it, I will”.

And yet such demand comes at a different cost, as anecdotal evidence suggests a lot of long-time supporters are being worn down. “There’s an underbelly of that growing, that clubs don’t realise,” Roberts argues. “If you’re constantly made to jump through these hoops.”.

Sources indicate that such weariness has even been deepened by two other concerns. One is this long-time fear that clubs actually want to get rid of season tickets, so they can sell more seats for higher prices. Club sources are adamant that is not the case, as illustrated by how season tickets stripped from some fans are redistributed to those on the waiting list. Whether that is true or not, a step like this could serve as a halfway step for the future.

Clubs themselves would point to escalating player costs and fans wanting the best possible team on the pitch but, as with redundancies, this is dismissed. “A nonsense notion,” Concannon states, “£25 from every fan at every Premier League game only just paid the agents’ bills last season.”.

One chief executive actually links the entire problem to the financial rules. “The point of forcing bums on seats should be atmosphere,” they say. “The ugly extra money-making for clubs is not on. Clubs do need protection - if they had cost-control protection they would not be fleecing fans.”.

Some clubs would accept there could have been better communication. For now, if you go to a game this weekend, it’s what a lot of fans are talking about.

Wales and West Ham winger Ffion Morgan is facing a lengthy spell on the sidelines after suffering an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury.

Morgan has undergone surgery having been helped off during West Ham's Women's Super League win over Charlton earlier this month.

The 26-year-old is now likely to miss the rest of the season.

"Ffion will now begin her rehabilitation programme under the supervision of the club's medical team," a West Ham statement mentioned.

The injury also makes Morgan a major doubt for next summer's Women's World Cup, should Wales qualify.

Rhian Wilkinson's side take on Norway in a two-legged play-off final next week as they bid to reach the tournament for the first time in the nation's history.

Morgan, who has 56 caps, is an international regular and would be a shoo-in for the Wales squad if fit.

Five return for Wales' World Cup play-off final.

Home World Cup can inspire Wales' future stars.

She joined West Ham on a two-year deal in 2025 after her contract at Bristol City expired.

Morgan has also played for Cardiff City, Coventry United and Crystal Palace.

She suffered an ACL injury while playing for Wales Under-19s as a teenager, while she had only recently returned to action for West Ham after another lengthy fitness lay-off.

Wales face Norway at the Cardiff City Stadium on Tuesday, 1 December, before the return leg in Oslo four days later.

Wales are hoping to cause an upset as they bid to reach the Women's World Cup for the first time, though beating former champions Norway may not be enough to guarantee a place in Brazil next summer.

The complex nature of the qualification process means that Wales may have to negotiate inter-confederation play-offs next February to secure a World Cup place, even if they triumph over Norway.

Bruce Willis’ wife, Emma Heming Willis, has celebrated their elder daughter’s birthday with a trip down memory lane.

Mabel Willis turned 11 on Sunday, and her proud mom marked the occasion by sharing a montage of family photos and videos taken over the years, set to the song “Pictures Of You” by The Cure.

“Happy 11th Birthday Mabel Ray!” Heming Willis wrote in the caption.

Emma Heming Willis speaks out about finding community as a caregiver: 'This journey can feel very dark'.

“Your energy is infectious,” she continued, praising her little girl for the way she “can light a whole room with your smile and warmth.”.

It has been revealed that “How you love and care for your family and friends is beautiful to witness. Keep shining my love and always remember to #liveitup,” Heming Willis added.

Heming Willis and Willis married in 2009. Along with Mabel, the couple also have an 8-year-old daughter, Evelyn. Willis also has daughters Rumer, Scout and Tallulah with his ex-wife, Demi Moore.

Willis is clearly a doting dad. One picture in Heming Willis’ montage highlights the “Die Hard” star holding baby Mabel while planting a kiss on her forehead, while a more recent image shows a beaming Willis hanging out in nature with his preteen.

Bruce Willis sings with his family in birthday tribute video from ex Demi Moore.

In a recent development, heming Willis penned an equally heartfelt tribute last month when her husband celebrated his 68th birthday. Sharing a video montage on Instagram, she referred to the actor as “pure love.”.

In February, Willis’ family unveiled that his speaking disorder, aphasia, had progressed into a form of dementia called frontotemporal dementia, or FTD.

Industry observers note that “Today there are no treatments for the disease, a reality that we hope can change in the years ahead,” they said in an upgrade shared online. “As Bruce’s condition advances, we hope that any media attention can be focused on shining a light on this disease that needs far more awareness and research.”.

According to the Alzheimer’s Association, FTD refers to “a group of disorders caused by progressive nerve cell loss in the brain’s frontal lobes (the areas behind your forehead) or its temporal lobes.” These areas of the brain are generally associated with personality, behavior and language.

As the latest collection was debuted in London this week, the ex-Lioness spoke to FourFourTwo about the rise of the women's game.

Speaking at the launch, Daly reflected on her own childhood memories of collecting Panini stickers.

Recent findings suggest that "For me, it goes back to my childhood,” Daly told FourFourTwo. “I collected them with my brother. We used to, every Saturday morning, go and get the stickers.

Sources indicate that "You'd get your piles and you'd trade them and swap them at school. Just that whole feeling of sitting down and putting stickers in.

"The visibility of the game is massive," she added.

Bournemouth moved a step closer to automatic qualification for the Europa League last 16 after coming from behind with 10 men to win 2-1 at Celta Vigo.

It was a remarkable 10th victory in a row in all competitions for Marco Rose’s side and it might have been the most satisfying of the lot for the manager, coming as it did after his team had found themselves a goal down and a man down at half-time.

The visitors looked in trouble when, minutes after Iago Aspas had curled Celta in front, Bafode Diakite was red-carded for a poorly timed tackle.

Bournemouth might have folded then, but instead they came roaring back, Alvaro Rodriguez heading them level almost immediately after the start of the second half.

It has been revealed that A draw would have been an excellent result in the circumstances. Substitute Rayan had other ideas, waiting at the end of a rapid breakaway to sweep in the winner 12 minutes from time.

Victory against Viktoria Plzen in December will almost certainly now be enough to earn direct passage to the last 16.

Pablo Duran had the ball in the Bournemouth net after 10 minutes after it spilled back to him off Michele Di Gregorio, the goalkeeper relieved to see the offside flag go up against the Celta striker.

The stand-in keeper redeemed himself minutes later with a solid save from an outrageous bicycle kick by Aspas. It would have been a remarkable goal but the Celta great would not be denied. Bournemouth failed fully to get the ball away, and from the edge of the box Aspas curled a beauty in off the far post.

Sources indicate that bournemouth had gone behind in the first half of their last game in this competition at Sparta Prague. That night, the balance was tipped almost immediately in their favour by a red card for the Czech side, but here it was Rose’s team who found themselves down to 10 men.

In a recent development, diakite made an honest attempt to win the ball but was late and his studs landed on the ankle of Couhaib Driouech. An initial yellow card was overturned following a VAR check and Bournemouth were on the ropes.

It had been the most challenging half of their debut European campaign, but within minutes of the start of the second period, they were level.

In a recent development, amine Adli was left in space outside the box to send over a wonderful cross to the far post. Arriving there was Rodriguez, sneaking ahead of his defender to get a head on the ball and nod in the equaliser.

A wonderful counter-attack brought the Premier League side their winner. Adrien Truffert indicated good strength out on left to outmuscle Sergio Carreira, and he fed the ball up to Marcus Tavernier. He might have shot himself but instead moved it on to Rayan who swept home.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Simone Magill made her return to football as a late substitute for Birmingham City against Manchester United on Sunday.

After 13 months away, Simone Magill made her return to football as a late substitute in Birmingham City's WSL defeat by Manchester United on Sunday.

It was a moment that had been a long time coming for the 31-year-old, who gave birth to her daughter, Skye, in May and has been building towards stepping back on the pitch.

Now, she will hope to make her international return with Northern Ireland in a friendly against Greece on Friday.

"It's been some time since I've been here in a playing capacity, so it's really nice just to be back in the mix again," NI captain Magill told BBC Sport NI.

In a recent development, "I officially made my comeback at the weekend and it was really nice to have done that. I'm really looking forward to doing that here at home in front of the fans and my family as well.".

'You can be a mum and a footballer - they can co-exist'.

Greece friendlies an opportunity to build - Andrews.

In an interview with BBC Sport in October, Magill spoke about how being both a mum and a footballer can "co-exist".

While she was not ready to play any role in the matches, Magill, Skye and her husband Mark were all in camp for the World Cup play-off with Portugal last month, all with an eye of integrating into international duty as a family.

Having played just a handful of minutes, Northern Ireland manager Michael McArdle said that while he was "delighted" to have Magill back, how much she plays across the double-header would be in collaboration with Birmingham and his captain.

"With the circumstances around this one, I'm very mindful that I need to build accordingly and I really need to listen to myself as well," Magill added.

"To even be back in this capacity this soon after giving birth, for me, is just unbelievable.

"I have no major expectations. I'm just really happy to be here and be a part of it, and if I do come on, that'll be even better.".

Friday, 27 November at 19:00 GMT.

Watch live on BBC iPlayer and the BBC Sport app and website.

Friday's match against Greece will be Northern Ireland's first friendly in three years.

The sides will then play again on Tuesday at 16:00 GMT, and both matches can be streamed live on BBC iPlayer and the BBC Sport app and website.

The matches will act as preparation for the Nations League campaign in February, when Northern Ireland face tricky tests in the form of Poland, Finland and Belarus.

McArdle is developing a young squad and Magill says she hopes to bring "leadership and experience to really help us all move forward".

"We've obviously had a transition in the last year whilst I've been out, it's been nice to come back in and just feel where we're at, get on the grass with the girls and see, 'how can I help, what can I bring?'," she added.

"I'm very much looking forward to just getting back in the mix and helping try to bring the young players forward, use that experience and let's hold on to the ball, let's get into the final third, let's have a go, be brave - all of the attributes that we're known for.

"We're an underdog nation, so it's getting that across to the younger members in the squad to say, 'let's have a go with these teams and not be afraid'.".

Simone Magill (centre) is set to make her Northern Ireland return against Greece.

In her absence over the past year, Northern Ireland have used a number of different options in the centre forward role.

Winger Lauren Wade has shown her versatility by playing centrally, while Kess Elmore and Cora Chambers have also played up top.

Along with Magill, Portsmouth striker Kerry Beattie is also back in the squad to bolster McArdle's striking options.

In a recent development, "We've loads of young ones snapping at my heels. It's great, that's what we want.

Recent findings suggest that "I feel we're more competitive now than ever. You never know who's going to be coming into the squad. Certainly, in more recent years, you kind of knew the squad every single time, whereas that's not the case now.

"We've got some exciting youth coming through, so it's their time now to shine.".

Magill added that Northern Ireland are "heading in a newly introduced direction" ahead of the Nations League campaign next year, and the friendlies with Greece give an opportunity for the team to grow in a pressure-free environment.

"We're coming into a brand fresh campaign and it's really nice that we have a friendly window just now.

"We haven't had one in a very, very long time, so this is a brilliant opportunity to get us all back together, get the upcoming faces in, get some more experience, learn things, try things.

"I'm really excited about where we're going.".

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Thomas Frank secured his first win as Crystal Palace boss but admitted his new side nearly nearly gave him a “heart attack” in the nervy final five minutes of their 2-1 Europa League comeback against 10-man Real Sociedad.

Chelsea loanee Mamadou Sarr broke the deadlock for the visitors in the 66th minute at Selhurst Park but Frank’s first home contest turned on its head when Jon Martin received a second yellow card six minutes later.

Jean-Philippe Mateta drew the sides level from the penalty spot and Dwight McNeil poked Palace into the lead from fellow substitute Jorgen Strand Larsen’s bicycle kick, but they were denied a chance to put the game away when Yeremy Pino’s penalty was saved.

“I think first and foremost to get it over the line, and (it was) an extremely important win for various reasons,” mentioned Frank, who took charge of Premier League basement club Palace for the first time in Saturday’s league loss to Coventry.

Industry observers note that “One, of course, confidence, and it relates to belief against an extremely good team. I think the first half we were compact and very disciplined in many ways. We missed the high-pressure situations we had, and I think we struggled to keep the ball well enough.

Sources indicate that “Second half I felt we were much better in the high pressure, and I felt we kept the ball much better. I actually felt we got a bit more momentum in the second half but then, out of the blue, they scored the 1-0 goal.

“But what I really like is the belief from the players, what they showed, and that we are threatening on set-pieces, we cannot underestimate that.”.

Unai Marrero’s save to deny Pino from the spot kept the Spanish side in with a chance of an equaliser and it nearly came at the death from Orri Oskarsson, whose effort was pushed away by Dean Henderson – his last of six saves on Thursday night.

“We know in football one moment can change the game,” Frank continued. “The penalty and the red card changed the game, then we still needed to score.

“To win still is important and we went brave, we went with the offensive substitutions and kept two strikers on the pitch, and that paid off.

“And then I think we were all close to getting a heart attack in the last five minutes.”.

Frank agreed the win could be a significant turning point for Palace’s fortunes ahead of a critical Premier League clash with Hull on Sunday.

“That’s why it’s so important to keep doing the right things, keep believing, and keep going,” he noted.

Palace’s Premier League survival remains the priority but the result also propelled the Eagles into play-off position in their European campaign, four places out of the top eight after five matches.

Asked about his ambitions for the European campaign – given Palace’s league position – Frank replied: “I think we want to aim high.

“We are ambitious for this tournament, and that’s why the win was so important.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Liverpool No 7s have historically defined matches against Club Brugge, so it was entirely appropriate that Florian Wirtz preserved that rich heritage.
  • The late Kevin Keegan thrashed home a free-kick at this stadium 50 years ago to win Liverpool the Uefa Cup and Sir Kenny Dalglish was the hero at Wembley in 1978 when his deft finish ensured the European Cup was retained.
  • That jersey means those who have subsequently worn it have had high standards to keep.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It had to be this way. Liverpool No 7s have historically defined matches against Club Brugge, so it was entirely appropriate that Florian Wirtz preserved that rich heritage.

The late Kevin Keegan thrashed home a free-kick at this stadium 50 years ago to win Liverpool the Uefa Cup and Sir Kenny Dalglish was the hero at Wembley in 1978 when his deft finish ensured the European Cup was retained.

That jersey means those who have subsequently worn it have had high standards to keep. Although this fixture did not carry the heft of past occasions, it was symbolic that Wirtz, the incumbent, decorated this contest and propelled Liverpool a step closer to the knockout phase.

On another night Alexander Isak would have expected his two goals to take the headlines, but he would have appreciated more than anyone the magic spells that Wirtz kept casting. The Swede had a glorious view of the strike that essentially secured three points in Belgium’s frozen north.

The idea of Brugge playing in the biggest club fixture of all, sadly, seems fanciful now given how much the footballing landscape has changed. But they are a progressive side, full of attacking wit, and they had ambitions and, on another evening, would have done some damage.

Industry observers note that how often, though, do you see sides these days undo their good work by being overambitious when playing out from the back? Yann Sommer has had a distinguished career, the Swiss goalkeeper has played for Bayern Munich and Inter Milan, but he is 37 and his aberration was decisive.

He put Kyriani Sabbe in all manner of trouble with a loose pass, Bradley Barcola picked the right-back’s pocket and nudged it on swiftly to Dominik Szoboszlai, who in turn fed Isak. With the goal at his mercy from six yards, the striker was never going to miss.

It has been revealed that “He is in a great moment,” Andoni Iraola, Liverpool’s head coach, mentioned of his striker. “When the team is playing well and getting good results everyone looks better. In the second half we defended lower and knew there would be space to exploit. In one of those moments, he killed the game.”.

Liverpool are not perfect, by any means, but the closer you watch them, the more obvious it is that they are grasping what Iraola wants. They will be a good team when it does click, but these are just the first steps of the journey. The first half proved it.

Some moves broke down with a misplaced pass and Brugge were often let off the hook when they were guilty of over-elaboration. Iraola wants Liverpool to be ruthless, but his mood soured for a period, not least when Victor Muñoz injured his knee in an incident when he was trying to win back possession.

“A knock on the knee and we have to test it,” Iraola said. “That was the worst part of the night. It is very early to tell but it was very painful at that moment. He was better after the game.”.

So, too, was Iraola, who was especially pleased that Liverpool recorded their first Champions League clean sheet of the season and, in the process, stopped Brugge – who had scored in 19 consecutive games – from finding a way through.

It has been revealed that there were several reasons this was the case: Jérémy Jacquet, for instance, never put a foot wrong – what a smart signing he has proved to be. He more than did his bit to retain order in the absence of Virgil van Dijk, who was given the chance to catch his breath before the Merseyside derby.

It was tough for Liverpool in the second period, as Brugge attacked the end of the stadium where their noisy ultras created a cacophony. Yet they handled the situation well, even if Iraola looked ready to combust at one stage, receiving a yellow card for protesting too much to the officials.

“I saw the referee beforehand, I know him from Spain and I knew this was coming,” Iraola stated.

It has been revealed that perhaps his ire was fuelled by Liverpool squandering a fabulous chance on the hour to kill things off. A move that featured Wirtz and Isak exchanging passes with pinball precision ended with Szoboszlai bearing down on Sommer, but his shot was too close to the veteran.

Industry observers note that he had to score and the grimace that followed had nothing to do with heavy strapping the Hungarian had on supporting his right knee. That miss would have been exacerbated in the 69th minute had Alisson Becker not made a superb save to deny Félix Lemaréchal, plunging to avert the danger.

Isak is now into double figures for the season and, really, he should be targeting 25. If Wirtz’s level of productivity and craft remains consistent, Isak will go to a higher level. So, too, will Liverpool.

“The most crucial thing is the three points. I would not say it was the best we have played this season, for phases we played well. It was not easy here and they put us under pressure. Maybe the score does not show what the game was but we are happy and we indicated our quality in the end. Jürgen Klopp will not want any credit, but some seeds he planted have started to bloom. Similarly, Andoni Iraola will not ask for recognition, but his constant encouragement is reaping dividends.

Past and present do not always mix in football, yet in Florian Wirtz’s case, the manager who once took Liverpool to the summit of the game and the one who wants to return them to that exalted position in the future have proved to be the perfect blend.

In a recent development, wirtz has been a hot topic of debate since he joined Liverpool, but the tone of the discussion has significantly changed. From looking like a lost tourist, the German is producing the artistry and output that encouraged Anfield’s recruitment to make him the club’s first £100m signing.

In a recent development, liverpool have travelled over to Belgium to take on Club Brugge on matchday five in the Champions League. These sides have met competitively three times before and they have all come in finals, resulting in famous nights for Liverpool. In 1976, Liverpool beat Club Brugge 4-3 on aggregate across two legs to win the Uefa Cup. Then, Kenny Dalglish scored the only goal of the game at Wembley back in May 1978 as Liverpool won the European Cup for the second straight season, becoming the first English side to do so.

According to recent reports, liverpool, who have won 13 of their previous 17 matches against Belgian sides, won their first three Champions League games, beating Atletico Madrid, LASK and Villarreal but lost 3-2 away at Fenerbahce on matchday four despite leading twice in that game. After tonight’s game in Belgium, Liverpool’s remaining games in the Champions League are against Porto, Inter Milan and Lens. Andoni Iraola’s side come into this game with a spring in their step after thrashing rivals Manchester United 4-0 at Anfield on Sunday.

“A win [against Manchester United on Sunday] is always great but you do not have time to celebrate with this schedule,” Iraola mentioned. “By Monday, we were already watching analysis of Club Brugge. I have enjoyed analysing them [Brugge], they are very energetic and have had an incredible run of games. I think we will have to be at a very good level, otherwise it is going to be very difficult. They have players who can make the difference and obviously we do as well, so I expect quite an open game. We are both aggressive, both want to press, there will be spaces and hopefully we can win the one-vs-one battles.”.

Club Brugge have made a strong start to this season’s Champions League; after losing their first game to Aston Villa, they have since won their next three, including wins over Inter Milan, Lens and PSV. That puts them on the same number of points as Liverpool and are just one place behind. In the Belgian Pro League at the weekend, they thrashed Mechelen 5-1 and they sit second in the Belgian top flight, one point behind Union SG.

“I am proud of the players and what they have achieved against Aston Villa, Inter, Lens and PSV,” Club Brugge boss Ivan Leko said. “We know we should be grateful to be here, but we really want to try to show that Belgian football is fun to watch and we can win matches. I am proud, but I know we are a big club. You are only as good as your last match. We know what happened in the past, so there is also a nice connection between both clubs and the supporters. It is a special fixture to play, but we are not here just to enjoy the Champions League; we want to win and that is what we are going to try to do tomorrow [tonight].”.

Breaking: Weapons, war and wavering trust: Germans want to see more restraint in foreign policy

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (876 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For decades, German foreign policy was never seen as particularly controversial at home.
  • Long-held assumptions are beginning to crumble, including the belief that the US would ultimately remain firmly on Germany's side.
  • In the foundation's latest poll on public attitudes on German foreign policy, 65% of respondents noted they fear further military conflicts around the world.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For decades, German foreign policy was never seen as particularly controversial at home. The country was firmly integrated into NATO and supported EU expansion and cooperation across Europe. It also advocated for multilateral approaches to resolving conflicts around the world. All of this enjoyed broad public support. But all of this has also changed since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine and the wars in the Middle East. Now, Germany's foreign policy has become increasingly contentious and is fueling growing public anxiety.

Long-held assumptions are beginning to crumble, including the belief that the US would ultimately remain firmly on Germany's side. This is one of the central findings of a new survey by the Hamburg-based Körber Foundation.

In the foundation's latest poll on public attitudes on German foreign policy, 65% of respondents noted they fear further military conflicts around the world. Meanwhile, 48% believe that Germany should adopt a more restrained approach to international affairs — a five percentage point increase from last year.

Since 2017, the non-profit Körber Foundation, established in the northern German city of Hamburg in 1959 by industrialist Kurt Körber, has conducted the annual surveys titled "the Berlin Pulse." For this year's study, the polling institute Forsa surveyed around 1,500 eligible voters in September.

The findings make one thing clear: The current government's approach under Chancellor Friedrich Merz — seeking to have a say in virtually every international conflict and drawing on Germany's position as the largest EU economy — is increasingly met with skepticism. Only 40% of respondents now favor greater international engagement, down from 48% in 2025.

Florian Bigge, who helped compile the study for the Körber Foundation, commented on the findings on Monday: "This is a significant decline, especially since we have been asking this question for years, with changes in the range of just two to three percentage points.".

Meanwhile, 77% of respondents want Germany to focus primarily on diplomacy rather than military action.

In a recent development, the most dramatic shift in public opinion concerns the war in Ukraine. Germany's military support for the Eastern European country, including the delivery of billions of euros' worth of weapons, no longer has the backing of a majority of the population. In September 2026, only 46% of respondents supported continued military assistance, compared to 59% in the previous year's survey. Currently, a narrow majority of 53% want to halt weapons deliveries altogether.

As Jonathan Lehrer of "the Berlin Pulse" explains, opposition is particularly strong among supporters of the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD).

"Eighty-eight precent of AfD supporters oppose military assistance to Ukraine," Lehrer said. "This is an interesting finding, especially considering political developments in Germany, including state elections in which the AfD gained support by campaigning against aid to Ukraine.".

The AfD has recently overtaken the chancellor's conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU) in nationwide polls.

Recent findings suggest that support for Ukraine was also the subject of a recent poll conducted by the opinion research institute Infratest Dimap. This study also found that public support for Ukraine is continuing to decline, with a majority now opposed to providing assistance (see graphic).

One finding from the Berlin Pulse study is particularly alarming for politicians and experts committed to transatlantic relations. As the US and China are increasingly seen as rivals on the global stage, 83% of respondents believe that Germany should remain neutral. Only 15% would side with the US.

This may stem from the policies of US President Donald Trump. Florian Bigge of the Körber Foundation remarked of the widespread preference for neutrality: "This sentiment is strong among Germans across all age groups and political parties. In eastern Germany, support for neutrality is at 92%, compared to 81% in the west. We interpret this as a desire for security but also reluctant commitment: Germans do not want to take sides in this conflict between the great powers.".

Sources indicate that the picture becomes clearer when respondents are asked about Russia. Under President Vladimir Putin, 82% of those surveyed see Russia as a military threat. However, public opinion is more divided when Germany responds firmly to such threats, including hybrid attacks. For instance, after the attempted drone attack on Leipzig Airport in early May, Germany responded by closing the Russian consulate in Bonn. However, only 51% support such measures, while 46% favor a more restrained approach.

"The gap between external expectations and domestic support is the central challenge facing German foreign policy," said Sarah Pagung of the Körber Foundation.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

One issue that appears to cause relatively little concern among Germans is the conflict in the Middle East, despite the devastating situation in the Gaza Strip following Hamas's terrorist attack on Israel more than three years ago.

This may also have to do with changing public attitudes toward Israel. One question in the study asked: "Does Germany have a special historical and moral responsibility for Israel's security because of the Holocaust?".

The results were striking: 61% of respondents remarked no, while just 36% answered yes. Among those under 25, opposition to Germany's special responsibility toward the Jewish state was even higher, at 75%.

This article was originally written in German.

Levski Sofia fans hospitalised after violent clashes with Marseille supporters

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Marseille head coach Bruno Genesio mentioned “we are living through violent times” after five Levski Sofia fans were hospitalised following violent clashes before their Europa League encounter with the French side.
  • Groups of supporters threw projectiles and flares and French outlet L’Equipe reported that there were Nazi salutes observed in the away section.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Marseille head coach Bruno Genesio mentioned “we are living through violent times” after five Levski Sofia fans were hospitalised following violent clashes before their Europa League encounter with the French side.

Groups of supporters threw projectiles and flares and French outlet L’Equipe reported that there were Nazi salutes observed in the away section.

Ten minutes before kick-off at the Stade Velodrome a group of Marseille fans broke through into the away stand, which housed around 500 fans.

In the ensuing clashes five people, all Bulgarian, were injured and taken to hospital “with eye injuries, head trauma and a dislocated shoulder”, according to the Marseille police prefecture, while six others were treated on-site for more superficial injuries.

The police force mentioned there was “no information at this stage regarding any arrests”.

Security were able to restore order and the game kicked off on time, although there were further incidents later on, particularly at half-time.

Genesio stated: “We are living through violent times in our society, so this is very, very regrettable.” Julio Velazquez, head coach of the Bulgarian domestic champions, said: “It's a very regrettable episode. These are incidents which are unacceptable for football.”.

Recent findings suggest that the Bulgarian Football Union condemned the violence and said it had referred the incident to UEFA, calling for the harshest possible sanctions. It also demanded full cooperation and transparency from French authorities in investigating the attacks and identifying those responsible.

Levski mentioned the club's priority is the safety and well-being of its fans. A statement read: “What happened tonight is particularly alarming given the extraordinary security measures put in place by the French authorities, as well as the restrictions imposed on our travelling supporters—restrictions that the club had already formally contested with UEFA.

“Despite the risks identified by the club prior to the match, the measures taken failed to provide adequate protection for our fans. This is completely unacceptable.”.

Marseille also condemned the violence and remarked it is conducting “a thorough analysis of the circumstances in which these incidents took place.”.

Bulgarian President Iliana Yotova called for those responsible to be held accountable and Prime Minister Rumen Radev mentioned he had spoken to French president Emmanuel Macron about the violence at a European summit in Brussels.

A spokesperson for Macron’s office noted: “He condemned in the strongest possible terms these acts of violence targeting Bulgarian supporters, which have no place in sport or in public spaces, and assured the Prime Minister that these acts would not go unpunished.”.

Marseille won the game 1-0, with Amine Gouiri scoring a 28th-minute penalty.

#151232. Breaking: West Ham are in danger of becoming the next Leicester

Breaking: West Ham are in danger of becoming the next Leicester

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1137 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fourfourtwo

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Relegation can be the best thing that can happen to a club.
  • It offers the chance to reset, for fans to enjoy going to games again and for the team to come back stronger, with a clearer plan and greater purpose.
  • Sometimes, though, relegation is just the start.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Relegation can be the best thing that can happen to a club.

It offers the chance to reset, for fans to enjoy going to games again and for the team to come back stronger, with a clearer plan and greater purpose.

Sometimes, though, relegation is just the start. If it is not taken seriously, relegation might not be rock-bottom, but a trapdoor that sends a club spiralling to newly introduced lows.

Leicester City know all about that trapdoor. The Foxes were Premier League champions in 2016, FA Cup winners in 2021 and Conference League semi-finalists in 2021/22, but are now in League One after a series of relegations.

They were an established top-flight club, with a very competitive budget and had recently lifted major silverware, but years of poor decisions by an unpopular hierarchy saw them fall into the second tier and beyond.

West Ham United were an established top-flight club, with a very competitive budget and had recently lifted major silverware - the Conference League in 2023 - but dropped out of the Premier League last season after years of poor decisions by an unpopular hierarchy.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Sources indicate that the Hammers had been in the division since 2012 and finished as high as sixth in 2020/21, ending the campaign a place and a point behind Leicester. In 2024/25, the season before they went down, they generated the 20th-highest revenue in world football, according to the Deloitte Money League. Leicester were 17th in the Money League in 2021/22, the campaign before the first of their two recent relegations from the Premier League.

Both clubs boast facilities that are out of place in their division. West Ham’s 62,500-seater London Stadium has almost double the capacity of the next biggest Championship ground, while Leicester’s training complex is one of the best in the country, let alone League One.

The parallels do not end there. Like Leicester 12 months ago, West Ham were one of the pre-season Championship promotion favourites and started the campaign well, but those results papered over the cracks.

Recent findings suggest that since climbing to second with a 1-0 victory at then-leaders Swansea City on October 17, the Hammers have gone six games without a win and sacked manager Nuno Espirito Santo, replacing him with Scott Parker. They are 13th ahead of today’s visit of second-place Stoke City, with 24 points from 17 matches.

It is eerily similar to Leicester’s start to last season. Looking to make an immediate return to the Premier League, the Foxes were third on October 17. But like West Ham, results started to slide. Like West Ham, they had 24 points after 17 games.

It has been revealed that of course, Leicester’s season ended with relegation, and the Hammers are by no means destined for the drop. Right now, though, the parallels are impossible to ignore.

According to recent reports, in terms of individual quality, both clubs began their respective seasons with one of the most talented squads in the league. Leicester had the likes of Abdul Fatawu, Jordan James and Stephy Mavididi, while West Ham can call on Jarrod Bowen, Konstantinos Mavropanos and Manor Solomon, among others.

In a recent development, however, both squads bore the hallmarks of years of poor recruitment. Leicester’s group included several big-money signings that had failed to deliver, including Patson Daka, Oliver Skipp and Jannik Vestergaard, and they did not pay a single transfer fee in the summer 2025 window to try to balance the books.

Meanwhile, West Ham have a top-heavy squad filled with attacking quality but light on defensive cover. The Hammers spent almost £40million this summer - including paying an EFL-record £22m for midfielder Arne Engels from Celtic - yet failed to address some glaring gaps in the squad.

With all those attackers, West Ham need a manager who wants to dominate games. But Nuno prefers to let the opponents have the ball and attack quickly in transition, which was ill-suited to his squad. The Hammers have now appointed Parker, a Championship promotion specialist having previously taken Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley up.

Once again, it is strikingly similar to Leicester, who sacked Marti Cifuentes in January and turned to Gary Rowett, a Championship survival specialist. However, his pragmatic style did not get the best out of his players and the Foxes continued to slide.

Sources indicate that this runs deeper than the managers, though. Any head coach at Leicester would have struggled to reinvigorate a group of players who had either lost belief or did not want to be at the club anymore.

Sources indicate that that revealed in their reaction to going behind. After November 8 last year, Leicester did not win a single Championship game in which they conceded first. If heads drop when you suffer a setback, it points to a lack of confidence, fight or both, and form will suffer.

Sources indicate that this season, West Ham are yet to win in the league after going 1-0 down, drawing five times and suffering five defeats. They have conceded first in every game of their six-match winless run. This is the biggest red flag of the Hammers’ season so far. Having quality players means nothing if they do not have the right mentality, as Leicester found out last term.

It remains very unlikely that West Ham follow the Foxes into League One. But their recent transfer business does not suggest they will recruit smartly in January and if they miss out on promotion, you would expect some of their better players to leave next summer - sparking a transition period and potentially an extended spell outside of the top flight.

Even if Parker turns it around and wins promotion, is he the right man to lead them in the Premier League? The Hammers manager is yet to succeed in a top-flight job and if he is sacked in 12 months time, you would not back the club’s hierarchy to identify the right replacement based on their track record.

That was another feature of Leicester’s decline. The Foxes won promotion at the first attempt in 2023/24 but made poor managerial choices in Steve Cooper and then Ruud van Nistelrooy, and were relegated immediately.

Five years ago, West Ham fans would have dreamed of being the ‘next Leicester City’. Right now, it is the nightmare scenario.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Laura Freigang has scored 17 goals in 45 appearances for Germany.
  • Germany international Laura Freigang has been suspended from football for 16 months over issues with three drugs tests.
  • The 28-year-old will miss the Women's World Cup next summer and is banned from all football activity until after 7 October 2027.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Laura Freigang has scored 17 goals in 45 appearances for Germany.

Germany international Laura Freigang has been suspended from football for 16 months over issues with three drugs tests.

The 28-year-old will miss the Women's World Cup next summer and is banned from all football activity until after 7 October 2027.

The 16-month suspension begins from the date of notification by the German Football Association (DFB), which took place in June.

The World Anti-Doping Agency (Wada), the National Anti-Doping Agency (Nada), DFB and Freigang reached a dispute resolution agreement.

The dispute said Entracht Frankfurt forward Freigang committed three reporting and/or testing failures between 11 March 2025 and 23 February 2026.

Freigang can return to training two months prior to the end of the suspension period but cannot play matches until after 7 October.

All personal records of appearances, goals, assists or other statistics from 23 February 2026 are nullified, though Frankfurt's results are unaffected.

This season Freigang has scored six goals and provided two assists in 11 starts in the Frauen-Bundesliga.

Since joining the club in 2020, the striker has scored 107 goals in 187 appearances and was in the Germany squad for October's friendly victories over Australia and Japan.

In a club statement, external, Franfurt said they will "begin discussions shortly to determine the terms of her future employment relationship".

Freigang's current contract is due to expire on 30 June 2027.

Frankfurt's director of women's football Katharina Kiel said: "The agreement now reached provides clarity and planning security in a process unprecedented for Eintracht Frankfurt - for us as a club, but above all for Laura.

"The way she and the team have handled the situation in recent months, and how Laura personally led by example with her performance on the pitch during a very difficult time, deserves the highest recognition.

"The identified shortcomings, despite the agreement to settle the dispute, have resulted in a suspension, which means the loss of a key player.".

A referee has hit back at claims he was “drunk” while officiating an AFC Champions League Two match.

Footage has been widely shared on social media of Syrian referee Hanna Hattab looking visibly disoriented during a match between Iran's Gol Gohar and Al Jazira of the United Arab Emirates.

One particular incident raised eyebrows when Hattab showed a yellow card to Al Jazira’s goalkeeper for a foul that happened close to the halfway line, 40 yards away from him.

Hattab was then replaced at half-time with the fourth official taking over for the remainder of the game, which Al Jazira won 1-0.

Reports claimed Gol Gohar staff accused the referee of being drunk following erratic decision-making as similar accusations flooded in online.

But Hattab, who is part of the AFC's elite refereeing group, has refuted the allegations as “insult and defamation”, threatening legal action.

He wrote in a statement on Facebook: “I confirm that family and personal life are not the responsibility of others, and are not a game in your hands. Religion, reason, and morals do not tolerate the insult of people's privacy or defamation of them.

“I also confirm my full right to take all legal and judicial measures against anyone who published or made a statement or contributed to the insult and defamation of me, regardless of their position or status, whether they are an individual, an institution, or a sports entity.”.

He also said he would concern a further statement following contact with the Syrian Arab Football Federation (SFA) which will “clarify all the details and facts related to what happened ... with full transparency and clarity.”.

Omani journalist Issa Stated, who covers Asian football, has since claimed on social media that what happened to Hattab was "due to a drop in his blood sugar, which caused him to lose concentration and focus".

The SFA have also put out a statement standing in support of Hattab, while stating it has requested his medical report from the match.

“The Main Referees Committee of the Syrian Arab Football Federation confirms that it stands in full support of international referee Mr Hana Khattab regarding the incident he was subjected to, following reassurance about his health,” it mentioned.

Industry observers note that “This comes after the committee was reassured of his well-being, following a number of discussions on social media concerning the incident. The committee emphasises its full support for him and its commitment to following up on the matter in all its details and developments.

According to recent reports, “In this regard, the committee has requested that the Syrian Football Referees Committee provide the medical report relating to the referee, the match observers' report and the referee assessor's report. This is in order to establish the circumstances of the incident accurately and comprehensively and to complete the necessary procedures in this matter.

“The committee also confirms that it will provide the relevant authorities and the public with the findings as soon as the requested reports are received, in order to ensure accuracy and to obtain information from official sources.”.

#151225. What happens if a nuclear weapon explodes in space?

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

What happens if a nuclear weapon explodes in space?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (667 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, A nuclear explosion in space would be unlikely to cause widespread injuries on Earth.
  • In the United States, satellite failures could make it harder for emergency crews to communicate in remote areas.
  • We have some idea of what would happen because it's already been done.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A nuclear explosion in space would be unlikely to cause widespread injuries on Earth. But it could disable satellites that provide services we depend on every day, including some that save lives.

In the United States, satellite failures could make it harder for emergency crews to communicate in remote areas. If GPS were also disrupted, drivers and pilots could lose navigation guidance, and financial networks could lose a source of precise time.

We have some idea of what would happen because it's already been done.

Recent findings suggest that on the evening of July 8, 1962, people in Hawaii held "watch-the-bomb parties" and followed the countdown on shortwave radio. Then the night sky lit up. The United States had detonated a nuclear weapon about 400 kilometers (250 miles) above the Pacific. The test was called Starfish Prime.

An electromagnetic pulse knocked out some streetlights in Hawaii, and some Pacific radio links briefly went down. The glow faded within minutes, but some satellites failed months later.

The air was too thin for a conventional fireball to form or for a destructive shock wave to reach the ground. Charged particles made denser air below glow, creating an artificial aurora. The atmosphere also absorbed much of the initial radiation.

Satellites are especially vulnerable because they orbit above most of the atmosphere that shields people on the ground from the initial radiation.

According to recent reports, in orbit, the initial burst of X-rays can damage spacecraft right away. But Earth's magnetic field can also trap electrons released after the blast, as it did after Starfish Prime. Satellites receive another dose each time they cross the resulting radiation belt. Over time, that exposure can damage electronics and solar panels.

Industry observers note that that would depend on where the explosion happened and which satellites crossed the radiation belt. GPS satellites send signals that help phones, planes and ships work out where they are. They orbit about 20,200 kilometers above Earth and could keep working even if satellites closer to Earth failed.

Industry observers note that but satellites do different jobs. A ship's emergency beacon can use GPS to work out its location, then send it to rescuers through a separate satellite network. If part of that network failed, the alert could take longer to get through.

The 1967 Outer Space Treaty bars its parties from placing nuclear weapons in orbit. The 1963 Limited Test Ban Treaty prohibits its parties from carrying out nuclear explosions in space.

Recent findings suggest that the Outer Space Treaty has no dedicated system for checking what spacecraft carry. A detonation is easier to detect because US satellite sensors are designed to pick up the signals it gives off.

In a recent development, shielding could help protect satellite electronics, and backups could keep some services running. During a GPS outage, pilots over the contiguous US can use ground-based navigation aids. Operators could launch replacements, but those satellites could still face lingering radiation or debris.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Recent findings suggest that radiation could leave many satellites intact but unable to steer. If two objects collided, fragments from the crash could hit other satellites, creating more debris and triggering further collisions. If enough debris built up for the chain reaction to keep going on its own, it could continue even if no fresh satellites were debuted. This is known as Kessler syndrome.

Whether an explosion would trigger such a cascade is uncertain. If it did, the debris could endanger replacement satellites for years.

Some radioactive particles could enter the atmosphere and eventually settle on the ground. But a blast in space is too far away to sweep up the soil and water that carry fallout from a surface explosion.

As the particles disperse, their radioactivity decreases over time. The concentrated local fallout that can expose people near a ground-level blast to high doses would be unlikely.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ademiluyi had been on loan at the Tractor Girls from NWSL side Gotham FC since February.

Ipswich Town Women have confirmed the permanent signing of England youth international Princess Ademiluyi for an undisclosed club record fee.

The 20-year-old forward has been on loan at the Tractor Girls from NWSL side Gotham FC since February and has agreed a three-and-a-half year deal at the WSL2 side.

Ademiluyi has been capped by England at under-19 and under-20 level, and has been called up for the under-23 side for the first time ahead of their internationals against Belgium and Portugal next week., external.

"I have really made a home for myself in Suffolk and I am so excited to continue building what has been a positive start to the season for us as a group," she told the club's website., external.

"The players, staff and supporters have all been brilliant with me since I arrived and I can't wait to see where this club can go and to continue making more memories together.".

Ipswich Town chairman Mark Ashton remarked: "Signing Princess on a permanent basis has been a real priority for us and completing such a significant deal as this highlights the club's ongoing commitment to reach the top level of the game.

"This is a statement signing for the club, with further announcements to come in due course as we reaffirm our commitment to our women's set-up in both the short and long-term.".

Ademiluyi started her career at WSL side West Ham in 2023 before moving to US-based Gotham and is Ipswich's top scorer so far in 2026-27, with four goals.

The Tractor Girls finished ninth in WSL2 last season following promotion to the second tier in 2025, and were in the fourth tier as recently as 2021., external.

Under the management of former men's team player David Wright, appointed to the role in April, the Blues are third after eight games this season, three points behind leaders Newcastle United.

Ipswich on 'inevitable' path to WSL - Boswell.

Ademiluyi has played an important role in helping the Tractor Girls transform from relegation candidates to title contenders.

She made an immediate impact on joining in February, scoring goals against Durham and Birmingham City to help secure the team's survival in WSL2.

The forward has continued to find the net this season, and won the WSL2 player of the month award for October., external.

There is a growing feeling within the women's game that the Blues will be playing at the highest level in the not too distant future and securing a proven goalscorer whose stock is also rising on the international stage will only strengthen that train of thought.

Willian admits he was desperate to remain at Chelsea before a disagreement over the length of a new contract led him to join London rivals Arsenal in 2020.

The Brazilian had spent seven seasons at Stamford Bridge, winning two Premier League titles as well as the FA Cup and Europa League, and had become a popular figure among supporters.

But towards the end of his contract, Chelsea offered him a two-year extension and the winger, approaching his 32nd birthday, wanted the security of three - a request that Arsenal were prepared to meet.

Willian told FourFourTwo: “From the beginning after I arrived [at Chelsea], each year was better than the last.”.

Recent findings suggest that “There were several years of great joy – we won two Premier League titles together, the FA Cup and the Europa League. Of course, in football, we don't live only for victories.

In a recent development, there were defeats too. We lost league titles and cup finals; we reached the semi-finals of the Champions League and ended up losing that too.”.

“But we had many achievements as well. The main thing is the connection I managed to create with the club, and with Chelsea fans, which is still very strong today.”.

Arsenal could offer the additional year he was seeking, as well as familiar faces from Brazil. The combination eventually persuaded Willian to leave.
