📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, an analysis of protein-coding DNA from more than 1.4 million people has identified hundreds of genes that influence a person’s height. Researchers identified 207 genes that were linked to a height difference of two centimetres, on average. They also identified 17 rare variants that prevent proteins from functioning, which have more striking effects. These include one variant associated with a 17-centimetre reduction in height and another with an 11-centimetre increase. The findings might help with the development of treatments that mitigate height changes caused by some medical conditions.

Sources indicate that the number of reported global cases of the viral disease dengue in 2024 — a 34-fold increase from the 430,000 reported in 1990. (Nature | 5 min read).

Reference: Research Square preprint (not peer reviewed).

According to recent reports, major prizes in economics, including the Nobel, are being awarded to researchers affiliated to an increasingly concentrated set of US universities. Just eight institutions dominate these top economics awards: Harvard University; the University of Chicago; Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT); Stanford University; Princeton University; Yale University; the University of California, Berkeley; and Columbia University. On the other hand, prizes in the natural sciences, engineering and social sciences outside economics have become less concentrated to certain institutions over the past 70 years.

Reference: National Bureau of Economic Research working paper (not peer reviewed).

Sources indicate that four years after NASA’s DART Earth-defence test mission smashed into an asteroid and succeeded in altering the space rock’s movement, a follow-up mission has confirmed it on camera. The European Space Agency has released the first images from its Hera mission, which show detailed views of the asteroid’s new crater. “Hera is a sort of Inspector Columbo going back to the crash scene to investigate what is the outcome of this impact,” says Patrick Michel, principal investigator of the Hera mission.

The New York Times | 7 min read.

In a recent development, this clip demonstrates the final five-and-a-half minutes of images leading up to the DART spacecraft's intentional collision with asteroid Dimorphos. This replay movie is 10 times faster than reality, except for the last six images, which are shown at the same rate that the spacecraft returned them. (NASA/Johns Hopkins APL).

According to recent reports, last week, the field of mathematics was rocked by two competing announcements about solving the Riemann hypothesis. The hypothesis is considered one of the most key open problems in maths. But if, like me, you have some trouble getting to grips with the famed conjecture — and what solving it could actually mean — Nature has you covered.

The hypothesis concerns the distribution of primes, and it is key because these numbers are central to all of maths. Riemann arrived at his idea by studying prime numbers as waves and, at its heart, it boils down to a statistical test. One that will be familiar to any scientist who’s ever analysed data.

Sources indicate that “If we can solve Riemann, what can’t we do?” says Xin Zhang, one of five mathematicians who spoke to Nature in the aftermath of the proofs’ publication. His reaction was one of excitement, despite Anthropic’s use of artificial-intelligence to develop its proof. But his enthusiasm was by no means universal. The format of Anthropic’s proof — 17 million lines of code with no natural-language version for humans to work with — is “the worst-case scenario”, says Álvaro Lozano-Robledo. And the shift towards AI-use in maths is “a choice to disempower ourselves”, says Tasmin Chu.

Bashyal observes a species of Coelogyne orchid, often found in tropical lowland forests and mountainous regions.Credit: CJ Karki for Nature.

Sources indicate that wildlife conservationist Reshu Bashyal works with people in Nepal to protect the more than 500 species of orchids that grow there. Prized for their ornamental value and uses in traditional medicine, hundreds of these flowering plants are illegally harvested and sold each year. But blanket bans on the orchid trade are unlikely to be effective, Bashyal claims, so more innovative strategies are required. One of these is an ‘anti-poaching taskforce’ that can document illegal activity, conduct patrols and spread information about the importance of conservation. (Nature | Leisurely scroll).

A biomedical innovation model that utilizes scientists in industry with government as their main funder could accelerate the development of therapeutics for common diseases that industry considers too risky to invest in, argue physician Victor Dzau, health-policy advisor Emily Shambaugh and healthcare entrepreneur Will Ellaissi. This government funding could operate at a national level, or several countries could form a consortium. Such a model “moves beyond the market-determined trajectory of research translation and ensures the public’s role in shaping the future of health,” the authors write.

Sources indicate that commensality — the act of sitting down to eat a meal with other people — has myriad health and social benefits, such as protecting against cognitive decline and helping us build trust with others. The presence of other people might also increase the enjoyment we get from eating. In an increasingly digital world, it might seem that opportunities to dine with others are dwindling. But research suggests that people are much more open and willing to accept invitations than we think, and simply putting ourselves out there might be an easy way to a dinner date.

Industry observers note that evolutionary biologist Pamela Yeh shares advice on how to navigate grief in the demanding environment of academia. (Nature | 8 min read).

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03894-3.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that "Over the past few months, goods and facilities worth several hundred million euros have gone up in smoke," reported Oliver Gierlichs, who heads Bayer's operations in Ukraine and serves as president of the German-Ukrainian Chamber of Industry and Commerce (AHK Ukraine).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Power plants, train stations, shopping centers, warehouses and residential buildings: The massive Russian attacks on civilian targets across Ukraine continue unabated. Industrial facilities have also come under fire, affecting German companies.

Industry observers note that "Over the past few months, goods and facilities worth several hundred million euros have gone up in smoke," reported Oliver Gierlichs, who heads Bayer's operations in Ukraine and serves as president of the German-Ukrainian Chamber of Industry and Commerce (AHK Ukraine). The damage is estimated at €500 million ($544 million).

Industry observers note that at the 9th German-Ukrainian Business Forum, held in Berlin on November 20, Gierlichs described the situation on the ground. Together with two other German business associations, the AHK had invited around 500 participants from politics and industry, including German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and Ukrainian Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi.

Industry observers note that according to the AHK, just over 2,000 German companies are active in Ukraine. German direct investment in the country totals around €1 billion ($1.1 billion). The situation remains critical due to the ongoing attacks, Gierlichs said. "We are preparing for a difficult winter.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

After posting comparatively strong growth rates in recent years, Ukraine's economy has slowed sharply since the summer.

"The intensified Russian attacks on Ukraine's critical infrastructure and production capacity in recent months have significantly worsened the economic outlook," according to the latest analysis by the Kyiv School of Economics (KSE), which warns of "substantial risks.".

Energy supplies are under strain, and electricity remains in short supply. Companies are also grappling with a worker shortage, as many people have been mobilized for military service or have fled abroad to escape the attacks. German business leaders also cite burdensome approval processes and unclear regulations in Ukraine.

In a recent development, "Not a single German manufacturer has left Ukraine since the start of this war," Merz emphasized at the business forum. He also pointed out that "in 2025, trade between Germany and Ukraine exceeded €12 billion, an increase of 4.4% compared with the previous year.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Military cooperation presently tops the agenda in German-Ukrainian relations. Germany continues to supply large quantities of defense equipment, but new capabilities are increasingly being developed through joint ventures. At the business forum, held at the House of German Business Associations in Berlin, the long-range combat drone "Anubis," produced by the German-Ukrainian joint venture Auterion Airlogix, was displayed in the foyer. The drone was developed in Ukraine and the software in Germany.

It has been revealed that A total of 5,000 drones are to be produced near Munich. This marks the first time Germany has established industrial-scale production of heavy attack drones on its own soil. "Through this cooperation, Germany's technological capacity for innovation is expanding in ways that would have been unimaginable just a few years ago," Merz remarked.

It has been revealed that the chancellor is convinced that cooperation between the two countries will also benefit Germany's civilian industries. "What we invest in Ukraine today will be repaid many times over through stability, export opportunities, joint projects, and economic growth," he stated.

Recent findings suggest that for foreign companies operating in Ukraine, it is a continuous balancing act. On the one hand, substantial risks persist; on the other, Ukraine represents a land of opportunity, with a market size virtually unmatched anywhere else in Europe. In February 2025, the European Commission and the Ukrainian government estimated that Ukraine would need $524 billion in funding for reconstruction and recovery over the following 10 years. This figure has likely grown even larger since then.

It has been revealed that in this context, Ukraine is increasingly seen not merely as a recipient of aid but also as a potential future business destination. The country aims to modernize its economy, bring it into alignment with EU standards, and achieve deeper integration into the European single market over the long term.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

"We see significant opportunities in the defense industry, the energy sector, infrastructure, information technology and many other industries," Ukrainian Prime Minister Koretskyi said in Berlin.

Recent findings suggest that "German expertise and Ukrainian drive, combined with unity and determination, make for a powerful partnership," Oliver Gierlichs noted. However, achieving this will require greater support, the AHK president emphasized. "Companies need reliable financing and investment guarantees, as well as effective instruments to protect themselves against war-related risks.".

Reliable logistics, predictable business conditions, and faster administrative procedures will also be essential, he added.

In a recent development, at the business forum, Chancellor Merz pledged support in these areas while also calling on Ukraine to pursue further reforms, particularly to strengthen the rule of law and combat corruption. "These reforms are a prerequisite for additional financial assistance and investment.".

Industry observers note that another challenge stems from the differing interests of the partners. German companies are seeking to expand into new markets, while their Ukrainian counterparts seek technology transfers and local production to keep as much value creation as possible in the country. "Export fees or legal restrictions on the transfer of intellectual property rights stand in the way of joint innovation efforts," the chancellor cautioned.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Representatives of Ukrainian business associations estimate that the private sector could cover up to 40% of Ukraine's reconstruction costs in the long term. For now, however, many projects rely on support from international development banks, government guarantees, or public funding programs. Without such support, many investments would be difficult to undertake.

In principle, business investment follows a straightforward model: Companies commit their own capital and bear the losses if a venture fails commercially. When bank loans are involved, the risk is initially shared by the company and the lending institution. Government-backed projects are different. When investment guarantees are in place, companies are compensated for any losses incurred.

This does not apply when companies incur losses as a result of their own business decisions. Compensation may, however, be available in cases involving political actions, such as expropriation, or when war destroys assets and disrupts operations. Under a government guarantee, the taxpayer ultimately bears the risk in such circumstances. By the end of 2025, the German government had provided investment guarantees covering a total investment volume of €558 million ($611 million) in Ukraine.

Recent findings suggest that german companies hoping to benefit from Ukraine's reconstruction need to establish partnerships and build a long-term presence in the country now. After all, the competition is already heating up. At the German-Ukrainian Business Forum, participants noted that German business leaders have often been more risk-averse than their counterparts from Turkey, India and China. International interest in Ukraine's reconstruction is considerable, and German companies are far from the only ones vying for contracts.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A upcoming study found a moderately higher risk of autism spectrum disorder in children born to pregnant people exposed to tap water with higher levels of lithium, but experts caution that this association does not show a direct link between the two.
  • About 1 in 36 children in the US is diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) each year, according to data from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
  • Recent findings suggest that scientists still don’t know the exact cause of autism, a developmental disorder.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A upcoming study found a moderately higher risk of autism spectrum disorder in children born to pregnant people exposed to tap water with higher levels of lithium, but experts caution that this association does not show a direct link between the two.

About 1 in 36 children in the US is diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) each year, according to data from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

Recent findings suggest that scientists still don’t know the exact cause of autism, a developmental disorder. Genetics may be a factor, but some have been looking at potential environmental causes, too.

Autism diagnosis has become more common, but pandemic disrupted early detection, CDC indicates.

Recent findings suggest that cases may be on the rise, but that is also unclear. One study published this year on cases in the New York-New Jersey area found that autism diagnosis rates tripled among certain age groups between 2000 and 2016. A 2021 report found similar increases in cases, but the CDC claims the increased number of cases is most likely linked to more doctors screening for the condition.

In a recent development, lithium is an alkali metal that can be found naturally in some food and ground water. It’s used in batteries, grease and air conditioners, as well as in the treatment of bipolar disorder and some blood disorders. Its levels in US drinking water are not regulated, according to the US Geological Survey.

A new study, published Monday in the journal JAMA Pediatrics, found a small association between lithium and autism diagnosis in Denmark, where the researchers say the level of lithium in drinking water is similar to that in American water systems.

It has been revealed that the researchers checked a database of people with psychiatric disorders for children born between 2000 and 2013 to find information on 8,842 cases of ASD and 43,864 participants who did not have ASD. They then measured the concentration of lithium in 151 public waterworks that served more than half of the Danish population and mapped out where pregnant people lived in relation.

For many neurodiverse people, 'The Sims' has been a lifelong comfort.

Sources indicate that as lithium levels in water increased, there was a modest increased risk of an ASD diagnosis. Specifically, compared with people at the lowest exposure level, those who had the second and third highest exposure during pregnancy had a 24% to 26% higher risk of ASD diagnosed in children. The group with the highest exposure had a 46% higher risk than those at the lowest level of exposure.

The researchers could not tell how much water the pregnant people drank, but they picked Denmark in part because residents there consume some of the lowest amounts of bottled water in Europe.

Experts say it’s important to note that the research can’t show that lithium exposure leads directly to an autism diagnosis.

Further study is required, said study co-author Dr. Beate Ritz, a professor of neurology in the David Geffen School of Medicine at UCLA, and a professor of epidemiology and environmental health at the UCLA Fielding School of Public Health.

Recent findings suggest that “Any drinking water contaminants that may affect the developing human brain deserve intense scrutiny,” Ritz said in a news release. She added that the research would need to be replicated in other countries to look for a similar connection.

The implications of the findings are complex as far as public health policy is concerned, according to an editorial published alongside the study. Lithium levels in water, at concentrations that the study associated with a potential ASD risk, have also been linked with health benefits such as lower rates of hospitalization for psychiatric disorders and suicide.

“If all these of associations are valid, the wisdom of Solomon will be required to develop guidelines for lithium in drinking water that are maximally protective of the entire population,” wrote Dr. David C. Bellinger, a professor of neurology and psychology at Harvard Medical School. “Until the basic biology of ASD is better understood, it will be difficult to distinguish causal from spurious associations.”.

'Heartbreaking' delays in autism diagnosis and treatment got even worse during pandemic.

It has been revealed that dr. Max Wiznitzer, director of the Rainbow Autism Center at University Hospitals Rainbow Babies and Children’s Hospital in Cleveland, points to other research on the effects of lithium on pregnant people who take it for mental health disorders. Those studies – which look at people exposed to much higher levels than are found in drinking water – do not show a connection with autism spectrum disorder.

“It’s an interesting association, but causation is definitely not proven,” said Wiznitzer, who was not involved in the new research. “We have to see if there’s a viable and biologically plausible mechanism by which a small amount of lithium in the water supply can somehow do this, yet pharmacologic dosing of lithium in women with bipolar disorder has not been reported to be causing increased risk of ASD.”.

Recent findings suggest that other studies have also suggested connections between ASD and environmental exposures to things like pesticides, air pollution and phthalates. But none of them points to any of these factors as a direct cause of the disorder.

In a recent development, A link between environmental exposure and ASD is hard to prove, Wiznitzer noted. With research showing that increased exposure to air pollution raises the risk of giving birth to a child with ASD, for example, he often wonders whether pollution is the determining factor or if it’s just the populations who live in more polluted areas.

“There’s a lot of speculation about about environmental factors, but how many of them are truly causally associated?” Wiznitzer stated. “We are bombarded with a variety of environmental stressors in our everyday lives. We have to figure out how to basically safely navigate them, and this is probably not one that’s high on our list.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Crystal Palace's Yeremy Pino has become the latest Premier League player to receive a yellow card suspension after accumulating five bookings since the 2026-27 season began.
  • Hull City's Matt Crooks and Aston Villa's Matty Cash were the first players to receive a ban for collecting five yellow cards before gameweek 19.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yeremy Pino is the latest Premier League player to receive a yellow-card suspension.

Crystal Palace's Yeremy Pino has become the latest Premier League player to receive a yellow card suspension after accumulating five bookings since the 2026-27 season began.

Hull City's Matt Crooks and Aston Villa's Matty Cash were the first players to receive a ban for collecting five yellow cards before gameweek 19.

Players receive a one-match suspension if they pick up five or more yellow cards prior to the conclusion of their team's 19th league match of the season.

There are now 17 players sitting on four bookings after 11 rounds of matches, meaning they must avoid another yellow card prior to the halfway point of the season to avoid a ban.

Bournemouth have the most players on the brink of a ban, with three players one yellow card away from suspension.

Sources indicate that after that date, the threshold increases to 10 yellow cards. Any player reaching that number before the end of their club's 32nd league match of the season will receive a two-match suspension.

From that point, there are further thresholds at 15 and 20 yellow cards.

According to recent reports, for players reaching 15 cautions, they incur a three-match suspension. Punishments for players reaching 20 yellow cards are determined by a regulatory commission.

Those cut-offs do not reset until the end of the Premier League season.

In the Championship, League One and League Two, there are similar thresholds.

However, with those three divisions having 46 rounds of league matches instead of 38, players have to avoid getting 10 yellow cards before the end of the 37th league match in order to not receive a two-match suspension.

In those divisions, the yellow cards are reset at the end of the league season and do not include matches in the play-offs.

The following players have received a one-match ban and will now receive a two-match ban if they reach ten bookings before game week 32:.

Yeremy Pino - Crystal Palace (five yellow cards).

Matt Crooks - Hull City (five yellow cards).

Matty Cash - Aston Villa (five).

If any of the following players receive another Premier League yellow card before the season's halfway point, they will be banned for one match:.

Vitaly Janelt - Brentford (four).

Oli McBurnie - Hull City (four).

Harry Maguire - Manchester United (four).

Pascal Gross - Brighton & Hove Albion (four).

Ethan Ampadu - Leeds United (four).

Oliver Boscagli - Brighton & Hove Albion (four).

Adam Smith - Bournemouth (four).

Marcus Tavernier - Bournemouth (four).

Antonio Silva - Bournemouth (four).

Alexis Mac Allister - Liverpool (four).

James McAtee - Nottingham Forest (four).

Chema Andres - Brighton & Hove Albion (four).

Bradley Barcola - Liverpool (four).

Murillo - Nottingham Forest (four).

The following players will miss their club's next set of fixtures:.

Yeremy Pino - Crytsal Palce (yellow card suspension).

Jean-Philippe Mateta - Crystal Palace (red card suspension).

Igor Thiago - Brentford (red card suspension).

Costinha - Brighton & Hove Albion (red card suspension).

Leny Yoro - Manchester United (red card suspension).

James Tarkowski - Everton (red card suspension).

💡 Key Takeaways

  • After 11 Women’s Super League games, Arsenal have just 15 points and sit sixth in the table, 12 points behind leaders Chelsea.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal would have already parted ways with Renee Slegers if this situation was happening with the men’s team, according to former Gunners striker Lianne Sanderson.

After 11 Women’s Super League games, Arsenal have just 15 points and sit sixth in the table, 12 points behind leaders Chelsea.

The Gunners’ latest setback came against West Ham, with a sixth home draw of the season, a result that left striker Alessia Russo in tears at the Emirates.

Sanderson was part of the Arsenal side that became European champions in 2007, with Slegers’ Arsenal side historically repeating the feat in May 2025.

The Dutch coach took charge on an interim basis following Jonas Eidevall’s departure, before being permanently appointed in January, becoming European champions four months later.

Following their triumph in Lisbon, they finished second in the league last campaign, four points off champions Manchester City.

“I've been a significant advocate for Renee to stay in the job, but I feel like after the Lyon game [a 2-0 home defeat in the Champions League], I just felt this feeling in my stomach that it’s time [to part ways],” Sanderson told FourFourTwo.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Industry observers note that “That was probably the most defeated I have felt. The players weren't fighting, they had just shown nothing, there was no identity.

In a recent development, “I love Renee, everyone loves Renee. But, I feel like if this was in the men's game, they'd have already cut ties.

“I actually feel gutted about the situation, because I have close ties and good relationships with everyone at Arsenal.

“The definition of insanity is doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results.

“Six weeks ago, I believed she could turn it around. But the reality is, we are now in another international break and it’s the same story. To be drawing with teams like West Ham, Birmingham and Crystal Palace is not acceptable, that’s no disrespect to those teams.”.

Arsenal made several additions to their squad including Lioness Georgia Stanway and World Cup and two-time Champions League winner Ona Batlle over the summer, but also lost a number of experienced players, including Katie McCabe and Beth Mead.

“There is something to be remarked about the types of personalities like Katie McCabe and Beth Mead,” Sanderson added. “Losing them is not the only reason Arsenal are struggling but Beth is a quiet type of leader and Katie is…you need a Katie in your team.

“Someone who is a nightmare to play against but will do anything it takes to win. You need those types of players. When I see Arsenal right now, I don’t see nastiness.

In a recent development, “My old captain, Jayne Ludlow, would do anything for us to win, putting your body on the line, and I'm not seeing that. Players have to take responsibility too.

“If Arsenal don't qualify for the Champions League, that will be a big, big, big blow.”.

If Arsenal were to part ways with Slegers, Sanderson pointed to Nick Cushing as a potential option for a replacement manager, also saying she would love someone like Canada manager Casey Stoney to come in.

It has been revealed that “Nick is the type of manager they need, someone with that personality,” she added. “I would welcome a personality like Nick Cushing, who knows what it takes to manage at the top and has good player management.”.

With Arsenal all but out of the title race, Sanderson believes it will go down to the wire between Manchester City and Chelsea, tipping the Blues to win it.

While she can’t see third-placed London City Lionesses winning this year, she is impressed by their upward trajectory and believes the side who signed Alexia Putellas in the summer are ahead of where they are expected to be and could be contenders next season.

London City owner Michele Kang also owns NWSL side Washington Spirit, who lost the Championship to Kansas City Current, missing out in the final for a third year running, leading to the dismissal of head coach Adrián González.

Sources indicate that “Michele Kang doesn't hang around,” Sanderson added. “Washington Spirit just lost at the weekend and the coach got fired the next day.

In a recent development, “The demand from her, it might be ruthless, but that's why she's successful. If Michele Kang was at Arsenal, this wouldn't be happening. That's the difference.”.

Lianne Sanderson was speaking to FourFourTwo via polymarket promo code.
